All of that. I actually paid someome else, so it required a bit of investment. We got our first webpage—or website, shall we say—up, and after a few weeks, it was performing quite well. However, it wasn't "selling" in terms of transactions; there was no e commerce on there. Its purpose was purely to drive people to the physical shop to see our products so they could call or email us, among other things. Within about two years alone, 50 percent of my business moved online. Meanwhile, many of my other friends opened multiple shops in different locations, believing they were doing well. For a time, that was true, until the High Street began to decline. What I observed was that the opportunities lay where the customers would be moving next, not necessarily where they had been for the last 50 year. That landscape is changing. You should always keep in mind: where will your customers be in the futuro? I believe there are two very important takeaways here. Thank you.
